To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oral administration of silibinin, an antioxidant flavonolignans, is safe and generates agent levels in blood, colorectal, and hepatic tissues that are consistent with the pharmacologic activity of silibinin in rodents.
repeated oral administration of silipid, a phosphatidyl choline formulation of silibinin, was safe and resulted in high levels of silibinins in the plasma, colorectal mucosa, and liver.

repeated oral administration of silipid, a silibinin formulation, to patients with colorectal cancer was safe and achieved silibinin levels of 0.2 to 4 μM in the plasma, and 0.2-2.5 nM/g in the liver, but 20-140 nM/g in colorectal tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new therapeutic targets for cancer prevention.
the development of a new class of anti-cancer agents.
the development of novel, safe, and effective chemopreventives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oral silibinin is safe and well tolerated and achieves levels in plasma, colorectal, and hepatic tissues sufficient to support further evaluation of its efficacy in human cancer chemoprevention trials.
the results support further investigation of oral silibin in human colorectal cancer.
oral silibinin at doses of 360 to 1440 mg/day is safe, achieves high concentrations in the plasma and colorectal tissue, and does not alter the levels of IGF-1 and IGFBP- 3 in the plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
silibinin is safe in colorectal cancer patients and is a promising agent for colorectal cancer prevention.
silibinin is a potent chemopreventative agent against intestinal cancer.

the levels of the agent achieved in the human tissues were consistent with the pharmacologic effects seen in rodents, but not the pharmacodynamic effects seen in human blood, which were not consistent with the pharmacokinetic effects seen in human colorectal tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oral administration of silipid, a formulation of silibinin, achieves high levels of silibinins in the blood, colorectal tissue, and liver, which is consistent with the agent's pharmacologic activity.
oral silibinin is safe and achieves levels in human blood, colorectal, and hepatic tissues that are consistent with pharmacologic effects observed in animal studies and in vitro studies.
the oral silibinin formulation silipide can achieve silibinin concentrations in the colorectal tissues that may be sufficient to inhibit intestinal tumorigenesis.
